text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- A small bomb went off near the centre of Riga, at a sports hall not far from the city council buildings. Two people were wounded. The police believe it may have been plastic explosive with a remote control.
- Estonian President Lennart Meri is to visit Latvia on October 23-24 for the first time since the two countries regained their independence.
- HELCOM, the Helsinki Committee of the Baltic Sea Environment Protection Committee, is to hold its annual meeting in Riga.

- The newspaper has an analytical article which says that former finance minister Aivars Kreituss was expelled from the Democratic Party Saimnieks because of his refusal to support the Riga chinaware plant, believed to have close links with the party's leadership.
- Zoja Golubeva from Riga has for the eighth time become the world draughts champion.
- The Bank of Latvia announces it will start using the SDR along with lats for interbank clearing payments. The bank's discount rate has been cut from 12 to 11 percent.
- Lithuanian citizens permanently residing in Latvia have started voting for the October 20 elections.
- Police arrested a person suspected of having robbed 25,000 marks and $5,000 from a currency exchange office in Riga after having killed its guard.

- The parliament leadership has assigned deputies Janis Adamsons and Juris Vidinsh to a trip to the Ingush Republic to investigate the situation of refugees from Chechnya. They received an invitation from the republic's parliament.
- Parliament is going to revise some laws banning non-citizens from holding certain jobs.
- Parliament will consider a no-confidence vote against Prime Minister Andris Shkele although it has little chance of succeeding.
